name: Maple Street
description: Two-bedroom apartment: open-plan living, galley kitchen behind a half-height partition, bedrooms off a central hall.

blueprint.layoutDescription: a two-bedroom apartment on one level, 12 metres wide east to west and 8 metres deep north to south, about 84 square metres internally, with a clear ceiling height of 2.6 metres over every room. One full-height wall runs north to south the whole depth of the plan, 6.3 metres in from the west end, and splits it in two: an open-plan west half holding the kitchen, the dining area and the living room as a single continuous volume, and an east half of separate rooms strung along a hallway. The front door is in the east external wall at mid-depth and opens straight into that hallway. The hallway is a corridor running east to west, 5.4 metres long and 1.18 metres wide, about 6.4 square metres, with no window of its own; the front door is at its east end, a door in its north wall opens into the primary bedroom, two doors in its south wall open into the second bedroom at the west end and the bathroom at the east end, and its west end is a cased opening 0.95 metres wide, with no door leaf in it, through the spine wall into the living room. The primary bedroom takes the whole north-east quarter, 5.4 by 3 metres, about 16.2 square metres, entered by that door in its south wall from the hallway; it has two windows 1.6 metres wide in its north wall and a third 1.8 metres wide in its east wall, a double bed 1.6 by 2 metres standing head to the north wall between the two north windows with a small bedside table on either side of it, and a tall wardrobe 2.2 metres long running down its west wall. The second bedroom is south of the hallway on the west side of the east half, 2.88 by 3.1 metres, about 8.9 square metres, entered by a door in its north wall from the hallway; it has one window 1.5 metres wide in its south wall, a bed 1.4 by 2 metres with its head toward the north wall, and a wardrobe 1.7 metres long against its east wall. The bathroom is the south-east corner room, 2.4 by 3.1 metres, about 7.4 square metres, entered by its own door in its north wall from the hallway, with a window 1.1 metres wide in its east wall, a bathtub 1.7 metres long set along the south wall, a basin against the west wall and a lavatory against the east wall. Through the cased opening at the west end of the hallway is the living room, which fills the whole south-west of the plan, 6 by 4.86 metres, about 29.2 square metres, running the full width of the west half; two windows 1.7 metres wide sit in its south wall and a wide window 2.2 metres long in its west wall, and it holds a sofa 2.6 metres long set against the south wall facing north, a rug 2.6 by 1.6 metres in front of it with a low coffee table on it, a long low sideboard 1.7 metres wide facing the sofa from the north side of the rug, and a single armchair east of the group turned to face west. Its whole north edge is open to the kitchen and the dining area, with no full-height wall anywhere along it. The dining area is the north-middle of the plan, 2.84 by 2.66 metres, about 7.6 square metres, walled only on the north where the exterior wall carries a window 1.6 metres wide; it is completely open west to the kitchen and completely open south to the living room, and it holds a dining table 1.6 by 0.9 metres with two chairs on its north side and two on its south. The kitchen is the north-west corner, 3.16 by 2.66 metres, about 8.4 square metres, worked as a galley: a counter run 3.05 metres long along its north wall with a sink toward the west end and a four-ring hob toward the east, a window 1.5 metres wide in the north wall above that sink, and a second counter run 1.8 metres long facing it across the galley on the south side. It is not a closed room — no full-height wall shuts it off. A half-height partition 2.16 metres long and 1.1 metres high, counter height, screens its south side from the living room and stops one metre short of the kitchen's east end, and that one-metre gap is the way in and out on foot; its east side is entirely open to the dining area. The floor is continuous throughout, every full-height wall runs the whole 2.6 metres from floor to ceiling apart from the kitchen partition, which stops at 1.1 metres and has open air above it, and the ceiling covers every space including the hallway.
blueprint.note: Prose is exhaustive on purpose: an earlier scene's shower room was never described and Marble simply did not build it. Every room here is named, sized, placed, connected and furnished, and the envelope repeats the drawing's own dimensions so the two cannot disagree.
